validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, active, FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas transmission pipeline. Confirmed via the original FERC certificate docket (Notice of Application, Docket Nos. CP03-302/303/304, filed May 20, 2003) and the Final EIS notice (Feb 2004, same docket family), plus a CURRENT (Sept 2024) FERC filing, Docket CP24-523 (Cheyenne Plains + Natural Gas Pipeline Co. of America joint lease application), which proves the line is still an active operating asset today, not a stale/phantom entry. Correctly classified transmission (not gathering/distribution): the FERC EIS describes 379.8 miles of 36-inch mainline plus laterals, compressor stations and 9 interstate interconnects -- unambiguous interstate transmission infrastructure. LENGTH (379.80 mi) and DIAMETER (36 in) are BOTH exactly matched by the FERC Final EIS (primary, 'A total of 379.8 miles of 36-inch-diameter mainline...') and independently by EIA's Historical Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (Miles=380, Diameter=36, Docket CP03-302) -- two independent origins, high confidence, no changes needed. Note for the record: Kinder Morgan's own current pipeline-operations page and Wikipedia both describe the CURRENT SYSTEM as '410 miles,' which is the mainline (379.8 mi) plus laterals added after 2004 (a ~21.4 mi Supply Lateral in 2006, plus three smaller laterals in the original EIS: 0.2 mi Sand Dune, 4.2 mi South Rattlesnake Creek, 3.0 mi Cossell Lake). Since this GEM row has no separate lateral rows and the FERC source explicitly labels 379.8 mi as the 'mainline,' the sheet's segment-level figure is the correct one to keep -- flagging only as context, not a defect. CAPACITY (800.00 MMcf/d) is CONFIRMED via a documented buildup across three FERC-approved phases, which sum EXACTLY to 800: Phase I mainline capacity 560 MMcf/d (EIA Historical Projects, Docket CP03-302, completed 2004-12-01) + Phase II expansion 170 MMcf/d (EIA, Docket CP04-345, completed 2005-11-07, matches industrialinfo.com/OGE Energy 10-K's cited post-Phase-II total of '730 mmscfd') + Kirk Compressor Station 70,000 Dth/d (FERC Notice of Application, Docket CP07-128, filed April 2, 2007: 'designed to transport up to 70,000 Dth per day on the Cheyenne Plains' mainline') = 560+170+70 = 800 MMcf/d exactly. Note EIA's own dataset lists the Kirk Station's added capacity as 90 MMcf/d rather than the FERC application's 70,000 Dth/d -- the primary FERC filing is preferred over EIA's secondary compiled figure, and it is the one that reconciles to GEM's current value. STATUS (operating) and FUEL (Gas) and PIPELINETYPE (transmission) are all straightforwardly correct and now sourced (see fills).

validity.recommendation: correct StartLocation/EndLocation -- the true origin is Cheyenne Hub in Weld County, CO (near Greeley/the CO-WY border area), and the true terminus is the delivery interconnects in Kiowa County, KS near Greensburg. 'Kit Carson' and 'Sherman' are the last CO county and first KS county the route crosses at the CO/KS state line -- roughly the MIDPOINT of the route, not either end.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Location [ref] cluster has StartLocation='Kit Carson' (Colorado) and EndLocation='Sherman' (Kansas). Per the FERC Final EIS's facility description, the route runs 189.0 mi through Colorado (Weld, Morgan, Washington, Yuma, and KIT CARSON counties, in that order west-to-east) and then 190.8 mi through Kansas (SHERMAN, Wallace, Logan, Scott, Lane, Finney, Hodgeman, Ford, and Kiowa counties, in that order west-to-east). Kit Carson is the LAST Colorado county before the state line and Sherman is the FIRST Kansas county after it -- i.e., they sit back-to-back at the CO/KS border, roughly in the MIDDLE of this 379.8-mile route, not at either terminus. The FERC EIS explicitly places the true receipt points/origin at the Cheyenne Hub in Weld County, Colorado (interconnects with Colorado Interstate Gas Co. and Wyoming Interstate Co.), and the true delivery points/terminus in Kiowa County, Kansas (interconnects with Southern Star Central, ANR Pipeline, Northern Natural Gas, Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line, and Kansas Gas Service), plus secondary delivery points in Scott and Ford counties. Kinder Morgan's own current operations page independently states the same shape: the system 'extends from near the Wyoming-Colorado border to South Central Kansas.' Trade press (industrialinfo.com) independently names the specific towns: 'originating in the Cheyenne Hub area of northern Colorado, near Greeley, and terminating near Greensburg, Kansas' -- Greensburg is the Kiowa County seat, consistent with the FERC EIS's Kiowa County delivery points. Three independent sources (FERC primary + KM operator page + industrialinfo trade press) agree the current Start/End fields are mid-route counties, not the actual termini. Candidate values given above use the town/hub names the sources actually name; a researcher should pick the exact facility-level point GEM's schema wants (Cheyenne Hub vs. a specific town name near it).

Searched FERC Federal Register notices (2003 application, 2003 draft EIS, 2004 final EIS, 2007 Kirk Compressor Station application, 2024 lease docket) and general web search for MAOP/operating pressure figures for Cheyenne Plains specifically -- none of the Federal Register summary notices state a pressure/MAOP figure (that level of detail typically lives in the full EIS/certificate order text or PHMSA inspection records, not the FR notice). No value found; leaving blank rather than inferring from pipe-grade/diameter.

The FERC Final EIS confirms the compressor stations use gas-turbine-driven compressors (two 10,310-hp turbine units at Cheyenne Hub, plus the 2007 Kirk Compressor Station's 10,310-hp unit), which are typically fueled by natural gas bled from the pipeline itself -- but no source explicitly states the compressor fuel type in so many words, so I am not inferring a value. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than guessing 'natural gas' without an explicit statement.

Two sources give CONFLICTING cost figures for the same original-mainline construction scope (380 mi, 36-inch, CO-KS): industrialinfo.com trade press states '$425 million investment,' while EIA's Historical Projects dataset states Cost (millions) = 410 for the same CP03-302 project. A ~3.7% disagreement between a compiled government dataset and a trade-press figure is not resolvable without the actual FERC certificate order's approved cost estimate (Docket CP03-302/303/304), which I could not access in full text (only the Federal Register summary notices, which don't state a cost figure). Per the standing rule not to force a number when sources disagree, leaving UNRESOLVED rather than picking one of the two conflicting figures. A future pass should pull the actual FERC order text (via eLibrary, not just the FR notice) to settle this.
